result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B lays out all five stages in one left-to-right row with 'what they do / what they feel' sections and promises 'what we can change' rows, so it reads as a timeline and gives staff something to act on. A's 3-column grid wraps onto a second row, which breaks the time order, and the visible part shows only issues, not what the studio owns. Both keep counts true to the six people, though B's 'Curious, but unsure' leans slightly toward invented feeling, and A's larger text is a little more legible. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A sets out all five stages side by side with 'what they do' and 'what they feel' rows, so the whole sequence reads at a glance like a journey map. Its subtitle also promises a 'what we can change' section for each stage, though that part is cut off in the screenshot. B marks its snags and the trial-class high more clearly with coloured, counted callouts, but its three-column grid wraps onto a second row, which makes the time order harder to scan. Neither shows a studio-owned fix within the visible area. Both get the counts right against the six conversations.
